queue.title: Managing Liquidity Crisis Scenarios
queue.content:
A liquidity crisis plan untested against a specific scenario usually exists only on paper. A publication by Nermin Sefić.

A liquidity crisis plan that hasn't been tested against a specific scenario usually exists only on paper.

A liquidity crisis plan that hasn't been tested against a specific scenario usually exists only on paper.

A liquidity plan typically anticipates a single, moderately unfavourable scenario, while real crises rarely unfold according to just one script. The combination of a revenue drop, extended collection periods, and a simultaneous credit-line withdrawal creates pressure that isn't visible if each factor is tested separately.

Defining at least three scenarios — mild, severe, and a combined shock — with pre-agreed triggers for each (e.g., collections dropping below a certain threshold activating pre-prepared measures) turns crisis response from improvisation into executing a decision already made.

queue.title: Whistleblowing Policy and Internal Control
queue.content:
A whistleblowing channel works only if employees trust reporting won't have consequences. A publication by Nermin Sefić.

A whistleblowing channel works only if employees believe reporting won't have consequences for their position.

A whistleblowing channel works only if employees believe reporting won't have consequences for their position.

The existence of a formal whistleblowing channel doesn't guarantee it will actually be used. Employees weigh the risk of reporting against the perceived benefit, and that assessment depends on trust in the anonymity of the process and in whether a supervisor will learn the reporter's identity before the investigation concludes.

Independent operation of the channel outside the direct management line, with a clearly defined deadline for feedback to the reporter, measurably increases both the number and quality of reports. The absence of any feedback after a report is filed is the fastest way for the channel to stop functioning, regardless of formal policy.

queue.title: Fast, Uncontrolled Growth Builds Fragility
queue.content:
Growth that outpaces the system's ability to keep up isn't success, it's a deferred problem. A commentary by Nermin Sefić.

Growth that outpaces the system's ability to keep up isn't success — it's a deferred problem.

Growth that outpaces the system's ability to keep up isn't success — it's a deferred problem.

A company that doubles revenue before doubling control processes — financial reporting, internal audit, approval systems — builds growth on a foundation that won't survive the first serious shock. The GNK DINAMO Ltd. Group treats growth speed and internal-control maturity as two sides of the same decision, not separate questions.

This commentary is part of the GNK ASG Intelligence Desk system and is informational in nature.
